items.stem: Two consecutive angles of a parallelogram are (x + 60)° and (2x + 30)°. What special name can you give to this parallelogram?
items.answer: Sum of consecutive angles of a parallelogram = 180° x + 60+ 2x + 30 = 180 ; 3x+ 90= 180 ; 3x= 180 -90 ; 3x = 90 ; x= (90)/(3) = 30 first angle = 30 + 60 = 90° second angle = 2 x 30 + 30 = 90° this parallelogram is a rectangle.

items.answer: let the smallest angle be x Other angle = x – 30 Opposite angles of parallelogram are equal Sum of all angles of parallelogram = 360 x+ (x-30) + x + (x-30) =360 4x – 60 = 360 4x = 360+60 = 420 x= (420)/(4) = 105 first angle = 105 second angle 105 – 30 = 75 third angle = 105 fourth angle = 105 – 30 = 75

items.stem: If the diagonals of a parallelogram are equal, then show that it is a rectangle.
items.answer: Given: Let ABCD be a parallelogram in which AC= BD To Prove : ABCD is a rectangle ; Proof: In ∆ ABC and ∆DCB AB= DC ( Opposite side of parallelogram ) BC = BC (common) ; AC = BD ( Given) ∆ ABC ≅∆DCB ( SSS congruency) ∠ABC = ∠DCB (CPCT) (1) Now AB ll DC (Opposite sides of parallelogram) ∠B +∠C = 180 (adjacent angle of parallelogram are supplementary) 2∠B = 180 ( from 1) ; ∠B= (180)/(2) = 90 ABCD is a parallelogram with one angle 90° ; Therefore, ABCD is a rectangle.

items.stem: PQRS is a parallelogram, in which PQ = 12 cm and its perimeter is 40 cm. Find the length of each side of the parallelogram
items.answer: PQ = SR (opp side of parallelogram) ; PQ+QR+SR+PS = 40cm 12 + QR+12+PS = 40 ; 24+QR+PS= 40 ; QR+PS = 40 -24 ; QR + PS = 16 ; 2QR= 16 (Opposite side of parallelogram ) ; QR = (16)/(2) = 8cm ; QR = PS =8cm

items.answer: ABCD is a rhombus ; ∠A =∠C = 70° (opposite angles are equal) ∠A+∠B = 180 (adjacent angles) ; 70+ ∠B = 180 ∠B = 180 -70 ; ∠B = 110°

items.stem: E and F are points on diagonal AC of a parallelogram ABCD such that AE = CF. Show that BFDE is a parallelogram.
items.answer: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram E and F are points on diagonal AC of parallelogram ABCD such that AE = CF To show: BFDE is a parallelogram. Construction: Join the other diagonal BD of the parallelogram. The diagonal BD meets AC at O Proof: OA = OC (diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other) ; OD = OB AE = CF (given) ; OA - AE = OE ; OC - CF = OF ; OE = OF ; Therefore, BFDE is a parallelogram as the diagonals EF and BD bisect each other at O.

items.stem: E is the mid-point of the side AD of the trapezium ABCD with AB || DC. A line through E drawn parallel to AB intersect BC at F. Show that F is the mid-point of BC.
items.answer: Given: ABCD is a trapezium ; E is the midpoint of the side AD with AB parallel to DC. ; A line through E drawn parallel to AB intersect BC at F. To show:F is the midpoint of BC ; Proof: AB ll CD and EF ll AB Therefore, EF ll DC ; In triangle ADC, ; E is the midpoint of AD EF ll DC (proved above) ; So, OE || DC O is the midpoint of AC (By converse of midpoint theorem) In triangle CBA, O is the midpoint of AC ; EF ll AB (given) So, OF || AB ; F is the midpoint of BC (By converse of midpoint theorem) Therefore, it is shown that F is the midpoint of BC.

items.stem: D, E and F are the mid-points of the sides BC, CA and AB, respectively of an equilateral triangle ABC. Show that ∆ DEF is also an equilateral triangle.
items.answer: Given, ABC is an equilateral triangle D, E and F are the midpoints of the sides BC, CA and AB To show: DEF is also an equilateral triangle Proof: In triangle ABC, E and F are the midpoints AC and AB EF || BC (by midpoint theorem) ; EF = ½ BC ------- (1) Similarly DF || AC, DF = ½ AC ----------- (2) ; DE || AB, DE = ½ AB ----------- (3) Since ABC is an equilateral triangle ; AB = BC = AC Dividing by 2, ; ½ AB = ½ BC = ½ AC ; From (1), (2) and (3) DE = EF = DF ; Therefore, DEF is an equilateral triangle.

items.stem: Show that the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular to each other.
items.answer: Given: ABCD is a rhomus To Prove: AC ⊥ BD ; Proof: Since ABCD is a rhombus AB = BC =CD =AD In ∆ AOB and ∆ BOC ; OA = OC (diagonal of parallelogram bisect) OB = OB (common) ; AB = CB (sides of a rhomus) ∆ AOB ≅∆ BOC (By SSS rule) ; ∠AOB = ∠COB (CPCT) (1) ∠AOB+∠COB = 180 (straight angle) 2∠AOB = 180 ; ∠AOB = 180 / 2 = 90 ∠AOB = ∠COD = 90 (Vertically opposite angle) ; ∠BOC = ∠AOD = 90 Therefore, diagonals of rhombus bisect each other at right angle

items.stem: Show that the quadrilateral formed by joining the mid-points the sides of a rhombus, taken in order, form a rectangle.
items.answer: Given: a rhombus ABCD and P, Q, R and S are the midpoints of the sides AB, BC, CD and AD. To prove: PQRS is a rectangle Construction: Join the diagonals AC and BD of the rhombus ABCD. Proof: In triangle ABD, Since S and P are the midpoints of the sides AD and AB. By midpoint theorem SP || BD ----------------- (1) ; SP = ½ BD --------------- (2) ; Similarly, RQ || BD RQ = ½ BD -------------- (3) ; From (2) and (3), SP = RQ Also, SP || RQ ; Therefore, PQRS is a parallelogram We know that the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. So, AC⊥ BD (4) ; In triangle BAC, ; PQ || AC --------------- (5) From (1), (4) and (5), ; SP ⊥PQ i.e., ∠SPQ = 90° ; We know that a rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. The opposite sides are parallel and equal to each other. Therefore, PQRS is a rectangle.

items.stem: A diagonal of a parallelogram bisects one of its angle. Prove that it will bisect its opposite angle also.
items.answer: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram and .,∠DAC = ∠CAB To prove: .,∠DCA = ∠ACB Proof: ∠CAB = ∠CAD ------------------ (1) (AC bisects angle A) The opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal. AB||CD and AC is a transversal, AD||BC and AC is transversal ∠CAB = ∠ACD ----------------- (2) (Alternate interior angles) ∠DAC = ∠ACB ----------------- (3) (Alternate interior angles) From (1), (2) and (3), ∠BCA = ∠DCA ; This implies AC bisects the opposite angle C.

items.stem: A square is inscribed in an isosceles right triangle so that the square and the triangle have one angle common. Show that the vertex of the square opposite the vertex of the common angle bisects the hypotenuse.
items.answer: Given: CAB is an isosceles triangle and ADEF is a square and ∠A = 900 To prove: CE = BE ; Proof: ABC is an isosceles triangle AB=AC -- (1) (sides of isosceles triangle) ; AD = AF (2) ( sides of a square) On subtracting (1) and (2), we get AB - AD = AC - AF ; BD = CF --------------- (3) In triangles CFE and BDE, ; DE = EF (side of a square) ; D = CF (proved above) ∠CFE = ∠EDB = 90° (angle of a square) ; ∆CFE ≅∆ BDE ( By SAS rule) CE = BE ( CPCT) HENCE PROVED

items.stem: In a parallelogram ABCD, AB = 10 cm and AD = 6 cm. The bisector of ∠A meets DC in E. AE and BC produced meet at F. Find the length of CF.
items.answer: Construction: Extend AD to H and join HF Solution: ABFH is a parallelogram AB || HF and HF = AB ; ∠AFH = ∠FAB ------(1) (alternate interior angles) ∠HAF = ∠FAB ----- (2) (AF is the bisector of ∠A) From (1) and (2), ∠AFH = ∠HAF HF = AH (sides opposite to equal angles are equal) HF = AB (opp sides of parallelogram) HF = 10 cm ; Since HF = AH, AH = 10 cm ; From the figure, AH = AD + DH ; 10 = 6 + DH ; DH = 10 – 6 ; DH = 4 cm CFHD is a parallelogram , We know that the opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal. ; So, DH = CF ; Therefore, CF = 4cm

items.stem: P, Q, R and S are respectively the mid-points of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA of a quadrilateral ABCD in which AC = BD. Prove that PQRS is a rhombus.
items.answer: Given: P, Q, R and S are respectively the mid-points of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA of a quadrilateral ABCD in which AC = BD ; To prove: PQRS is a rhombus Proof: In triangle ADC, S and R are the midpoints of AD and DC SR || AC, SR = ½ AC(1) (By midpoint theorem) ; In triangle ABC, P and Q are the midpoints of AB and BC ; PQ || AC, PQ = ½ AC --------(2) (By midpoint theorem) Comparing (1) and (2), SR = PQ = ½ AC ----------- (3) ; In triangle BCD, RQ || BD, RQ = ½ BD --------(4) (By midpoint theorem) , In triangle BAD, ; SP || BD SP = ½ BD -----------(5) (By midpoint theorem) Comparing (4) and (5), SP = RQ = ½ BD ----------- (6) AC = BD (given) Dividing by 2 on both sides, ½ AC = ½ BD ; From (3) and (6), SR = PQ = SP = RQ ; This implies all the sides of the quadrilateral are equal. Therefore, PQRS is a rhombus.
